51580730.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Enterococcus faecalis type 1 MetRS expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) cells assessed as dissociation constant by ITC analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC assay: The binding affinity of compounds to MetRS proteins were measured using a MicroCal PEAQ-ITC microcalorimeter (Malvern Panalytical). CHX and its derivative at the concentration of 200 μM were titrated to 20 μM MetRS in the buffer containing 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl and 5% glycerol. To investigate the influence of ATP on compound binding, the compound and MetRS were pre-incubated with the same concentrations of ATP. The titrations were conducted at the temperature of 25 °C, with 0.2 μL for the first injection and 2 μL for the following 18 drops. The interval between two injections is 150 s. The dissociation constant (Kd) was determined by fitting the calorimetric data to a one-site binding model using MicroCal PEAQ-ITC analysis software.

original_paragraph.Results Section - 3.3 CHX selectively in: Compared to SaMetRS, the inhibition against EfMetRS by CHX was even stronger, with an IC50 of 8.5 ± 1.0 μM (in 50 μM ATP) and a Kd of 0.30 ± 0.04 μM (in 1 mM ATP) (Fig. 4 and S3B). In contrast, the inhibition of CHX to type 2 MetRS from human cytoplasm and Gram-negative S. enterica and E. coli was minimal (Fig. 4C–E). Consistently, the ITC titrations showed that CHX exclusively binds to type 1 MetRS but not type 2 MetRS, regardless of the presence of ATP (Figs. 2C and 4F–M). These results demonstrated that CHX is selective binder and inhibitor of type 1 MetRS.
